content: JSONLs are the canonical bearer of project knowledge. The agent explicitly keeps all durable knowledge from kindex.db represented losslessly in canonical JSONLs after captures, edits and links. SQLite databases are disposable caches. Worktrees may disappear outside our control; no correctness guarantee depends on database preservation, archival, merging, rescue or a teardown step. Optional database merging is an optimization only. This is user-authorized prompt/docs guidance, not automatic runtime enforcement. Best-effort cleanup is encouraged when available, never required. Reconstruct disposable state from surviving canonical knowledge even when cleanup did not happen. Prompts alone cannot guarantee persistence or recovery; explicitly disclose unrecoverable never-persisted knowledge. Expected data loss is a failure mode, not a desired outcome.

content: Users should prompt their agent to ensure all existing kindex.db knowledge is maintained in JSONLs. Inventory all durable records, complete content, metadata, lifecycle, relationships and directions, provenance and source bindings; compare field-by-field with canonical sources, preserve independent source knowledge, reconcile legacy JSON and JSONL explicitly, honor privacy, and report precise unsupported types or reader limitations. Summary indexes and selected repo-memory publications alone are not lossless migrations. The guide is docs/canonical-knowledge-migration.md and the unreleased changelog includes a copyable migration prompt. User clarification permits intentional migration loss explicitly described in release notes with omitted knowledge/bindings, scope, reasons and consequences. Report retained coverage and intentional exclusions separately; never claim excluded knowledge was losslessly migrated or label accidental ongoing loss intentional.

content: Reassessed against user acceptance of intentional, release-documented migration loss. PR69 d139e6d deliberately gives existing knowledge.json precedence: with both formats present, import reads JSON only and excludes JSONL-only records without deleting their bytes. No automatic union, dual-write or old-client JSONL support is promised; explicit agent reconciliation is the migration path. This documented compatibility limitation is accepted, not a defect or automatic merge blocker; a coexistence diagnostic is optional. PR71 does not retroactively reconstruct legacy expired-session source bindings; unresolved historical provenance is documented, and agents may reconstruct only from verifiable canonical evidence. Separately, the prior relationship-only learn coverage gap is fixed by PR71 ea8a42f: supplied source records survive on learned-text evidence documents linked to matched concepts and valid relationship endpoints, including replay. Base behavior also gated documents on new concepts and did not save structured refs: incomplete coverage of the new guarantee, not a previously working behavior regression or intentional migration exclusion. Disposable worktree/cache deletion and lack of rescue are not defects. Absence of cleanup is expected, but surviving canonical knowledge still requires a recovery path. Current graph_transfer export/import filters extra to LIFECYCLE_KEYS and excludes source_refs; PR71 has no canonical JSONL source resolver/rebinding and fresh rebuilt caches have new UUIDs. These concrete recovery gaps require separately scoped runtime work and are not accepted intentional migration exclusions. Snapshot merge selects same-ID index conflicts by timestamp (ties ours), code-map collisions can keep ours: reconcile canonical sources/references before regeneration; do not claim lossless snapshot merging.
